claim.text: Rust-only Prolog can execute disjunction with comma precedence and invocation-scoped cut, preserving caller alternatives and later-created choices
claim.scope: finite-term Horn+control subset, ten scoped-control unit tests plus two CLI cases, Linux ELF64 and i686 ELF32
assumptions: DFS alternative states stored on one LIFO stack
Pending goal retains owning predicate barrier when returning to caller
Substitutions are cloned per choice state, not trailed
Rust-only binary, no C Prolog runtime dependency
forbidden_promotions: Do not claim WAM heap, trail or native Prolog compiler implemented
Do not claim complete ISO cut semantics for meta-call, modules, if-then and exceptions
Do not treat project-authored expected answers as independent third-party replication
Do not infer speedup or memory safety from passing functional cases

specification.intended_object: Scoped choicepoint barrier embedded in each pending goal with correct semicolon/comma control expression parse
invariants: Comma binds tighter than semicolon and grouping overrides precedence
Root cut prunes earlier query alternatives
Cut after disjunction commits earlier branch and clause alternatives
Cut before disjunction retains later choices
Inner predicate cut does not prune earlier caller choicepoints
Caller cut can prune child alternatives when returning
A cut followed by fail still commits, without reaching fallback clauses
